qt: to the Council Damien Carême (The Left), Martin Schirdewan (The Left) Subject:

In response to written question E-004872/20251 on national terrorism lists2, the Commission stated that listing under Council Common Position 2001/931/CFSP3 requires a decision by a competent authority on the involvement of the person or entity in a terrorist act, as defined in Article 1(3). It also stated that listing decisions rest with the Council acting unanimously and that assessing whether the Hungarian Government Decree 297/2025 (IX.26.)4 meets the requirements in question ‘ultimately rests with the Council’. The decree, which designates ‘Antifa’ as a terrorist organisation without any prior conviction or judicial finding against the groups concerned, has not been repealed by the new Hungarian Government led by Prime Minister Péter Magyar. 1.

Has the Council assessed whether Decree 297/2025 (IX.26.) constitutes a decision by a competent authority within the meaning of Council Common Position 2001/931/CFSP, and does it consider that the decree meets the requirements for listing under that instrument?

Does the Council consider that the attribution of violent acts to individuals who have not been convicted, in the recitals of a government decree, is compatible with the values set out in Article 2 of the Treaty on European Union, including the presumption of innocence and judicial independence, and does it intend to address this matter in its rule of law dialogue?
Will the Council call on the Hungarian Government to repeal the decree?
